items: Scope of observable result: for every valid invocation of shiftPitchLinear, the only caller-visible result that participates in the allowed-result relation is the output buffer content at logical coordinates (x, y) with 0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height, where the output row stride is pitch elements. Storage locations outside those logical coordinates, including pitch padding columns x in [width, pitch), are not constrained by and do not participate in the allowed-result relation.

Elementwise result relation: for each valid logical output coordinate (x, y), the output element must be exactly the binary32 value located at input logical coordinate (ix, iy) = (floor_mod(x + shiftX, width), floor_mod(y + shiftY, height)). Exact IEEE-754 binary32 equality is required; tolerance-based or approximate comparisons are not part of the allowed-result relation.

Input source relation: the input element for logical coordinate (ix, iy) is the binary32 at row iy and column ix of the readable input's logical width-by-height region in the pitch-linear layout used by the invocation, with 0 <= ix < width and 0 <= iy < height. Values outside that logical region, including pitch padding bytes, must not be observable in the constrained output coordinates.

Index mapping: floor_mod(a, n) is the mathematical floor-modulo function for positive n, defined as floor_mod(a, n) = ((a mod n) + n) mod n, yielding a value in [0, n-1]. The relation must hold for every shift value allowed by the domain, including cases where x + shiftX or y + shiftY is negative.

Valid-domain boundary: width > 0, height > 0, pitch >= width, the output storage is writable for height rows of pitch elements, the input storage is readable for the corresponding logical width-by-height region, and x + shiftX and y + shiftY are representable in the integer coordinate arithmetic used to derive the mathematical floor-modulo indices. Outside this domain no allowed-result relation is asserted.

Implementation freedom: any implementation that produces the exact output permutation defined above is allowed whether it uses CUDA normalized-coordinate texture reads, cudaTextureObject_t, wrap address mode, point filtering, a different launch configuration, or a direct index computation. Conversely, those implementation mechanisms do not relax or expand the required exact output relation.

Relation exhaustion: the allowed-result relation is exhausted by the exact output permutation described above; the sample harness's timing, bandwidth, fetch-rate, and console-text outputs are not part of the preserved observable semantics of shiftPitchLinear.
